description: Only one panel of this three-part figure group is supplied: a grayscale metallographic micrograph labelled "(a)" in the top-left corner, with a black square scale bar labelled "40 µm" in the bottom-right corner. The field shows a fully equiaxed, polygonal grain structure with straight-to-slightly-curved grain boundaries, imaged in uniform light grey; a second, darker grey population of blocky and irregularly shaped regions is scattered heterogeneously through the field, and numerous small black dots (etch pits or fine particles) are dispersed both inside grains and along boundaries. No crystallographic colouring, legend, axis or magnification is printed; no numeric values other than the "40 µm" scale bar are visible. The caption states that (a) is the ferritic family of high-Al steels, that (b) is a two-phase austenite (red)–ferrite EBSD image and (c) a three-phase austenite–ferrite (blue) EBSD image, with κ-phase too small to be observed; panels (b) and (c) were not provided, so the group's EBSD part cannot be verified here. The arguing point of the supplied panel is that one family of high-Al steels is essentially single-phase ferritic with equiaxed grains.

subfigures.description: Grayscale micrograph of an equiaxed, polygonal ferritic grain structure with a dispersed darker grey second-phase/constituent population and fine black dots; black square scale bar labelled "40 µm" at bottom right. The caption identifies this as the ferritic high-Al steel family.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a grayscale micrograph showing equiaxed polygonal grains with well-defined boundaries in a light-grey matrix.
A black square scale bar in the bottom-right corner of (a) is labelled "40 µm".
A darker grey population of blocky, irregular regions is heterogeneously distributed through the matrix of (a), and small black dots are dispersed intra- and intergranularly.
The caption states that (a) corresponds to the ferritic family of high-Al steels.

The caption states that the last two images of the group, (b) two-phase austenite (red)–ferrite and (c) three-phase austenite–ferrite (blue), are electron backscattered diffraction (EBSD) images; these panels are not present in the supplied image.
The caption states that the phase it writes as "j-phase" is not observed in these microstructures because of its size.

The citing text classifies high-Al automotive steels into three families: ferritic Fe-Al alloys (Fig. 5a), two-phase austenite-ferrite alloys with C and Mn stabilising austenite (Fig. 5b, austenite in red), and austenitic alloys with relatively high C and Mn (Fig. 5c).

The citing text states that the third family has been called TRIPLEX because of the additional small amount of ferrite (Fig. 5c, ferrite in blue) and intragranular nanometric precipitation of the j-phase.
No axis, legend, magnification value, etchant or composition label is printed on panel (a); the only numeric annotation is the "40 µm" scale bar.

phase identity of the darker grey blocky constituent in (a) is not labelled, unreadable/undetermined from the image
